case.pattern_description: A stolen card number is cashed out through a tight run of online purchases, each priced just under $500, apparently to stay below a per-transaction authorization or review limit. The same template appears on 15 other customers' cards within three weeks and the bank's model scores it low, so it is repeated, coordinated abuse rather than a one-off. It was found by matching the burst shape across cards and against earlier confirmed cases.

evidence.claim: 4 online purchases of $456.96 to $488.04 within 30 minutes, each just under $500; before this burst the card's largest online purchase was $50.01
Customer C07297 disputes transaction 3476682 ($482.12); in the bank's closed cases every customer-reported alert was confirmed fraud
The same template (three or more online purchases just under $500 within 40 minutes) appears on 15 other cards within three weeks
Online purchase on a card whose history is 97% in person (199 earlier transactions)

Identity record marks the device (Trident/7.0 | Windows 7 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080) as New for this account; 100% of the card's earlier online purchases were also from New devices (in the closed cases a New device is not more common in fraud than in normal traffic for this product)

Policy applied, Fraud Policy R9: Undocumented patterns: When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend CREATE_CASE, FILE_REPORT, and ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST, and describe the pattern in your own words.

Nearest documented pattern by text similarity is Known fraud patterns: Card-not-present fraud (cosine 0.81), which does not describe a coordinated template across customers; its definition: The number is used online without the card.

case.summary: The alert was triggered when customer C07297 reported that they never made the $482.12 online purchase (transaction 3476682) on their Mastercard debit card. The strongest findings are a burst of four online purchases between $456.96 and $488.04 within a 30-minute window, each just under the $500 threshold, a sudden increase from the card's previous maximum online purchase of $50.01, and the fact that this pattern of three or more sub-threshold purchases within 40 minutes has been seen on fifteen other cards in the past three weeks. The case was judged to be fraud with a probability of 97 percent. The recommended actions are to block the card, create a case file, file a report, and escalate the matter to an analyst.

sar.narrative: This report concerns customer C07297, card C07297-K1, issued as a mastercard debit. On 2016-11-21, 4 transaction(s) totalling $1,906.07 were identified as part of one fraud episode, beginning with transaction 3476602. The activity took place online, product code(s) C, billing region(s) 264, 476, from device profile(s) Trident/7.0 | Windows 7 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080; iOS Device | iOS 11.2.1 | mobile safari 11.0 | 2208x1242. The transactions were a burst of online purchases priced just under a round limit. The activity is assessed as an undocumented coordinated pattern: 4 online purchases of $456.96 to $488.04 within 30 minutes, each just under $500; before this burst the card's largest online purchase was $50.01; Customer C07297 disputes transaction 3476682 ($482.12); in the bank's closed cases every customer-reported alert was confirmed fraud; The same template (three or more online purchases just under $500 within 40 minutes) appears on 15 other cards within three weeks. No other cardholder was found to share a device profile, region cluster or email with this activity. Earlier confirmed cases CC-4124, CC-3748, CC-3907 show the same pattern. The cardholder reported the disputed transaction to the bank and denied making it. The bank has recommended BLOCK_CARD and opened an internal case; the report is filed under R9, §3a.

stop_reason: Fraud probability 0.97 is at or above 0.85 with 3 independent evidence groups (sequence, network, customer), so section 6 allows a decision without asking the customer; further queries would not change the actions.
